title: What to Plant

source.title: As US midterms approach, farmers decide what to plant and how to vote
source.note: published 10-29 14:25 UTC; the 10-29 sweep matched it on 'midterm' ONLY — the feed carried no opening, so 'diesel' (¶14), 'fuel' (¶4, ¶16) and 'Strait of Hormuz' (¶13) were not seen by the sweep; found by reading the page. Read in full via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over twelve words. A reported feature from northeast Arkansas: the article, two farmers (one a Senate candidate), an extension economist, a political scientist. Chosen as the only AJ page in today's queue on a live object (the others: Finland/Google, sports owners, the megadonors video); my call

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c) read as a farm input, from outside the US horizon — diesel 72% over budget and urea 39% over across the seasons (¶14, a University of Arkansas extension budget), the Strait's closure named as the cause of the spring jump (¶13, H6 marked), about $343m of added cost for Arkansas alone (¶15), and the holder's relief on the page as cash — the $8bn fuel relief program (¶16), under half of the estimate. The deal, Russia, the cargo and the pump are not on the page; the price is a crop plan (rice to soya) and a vote

zAxis.pos: prices come down by the deal — and the farm's diesel line comes back to budget before the next planting
zAxis.neg: they do not — diesel ran 72% over budget, the relief is cash rather than a price, and the crop plan changes

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11), restated as 'really fast' on the same day's Fox page. This page is the first on the Press to carry diesel — the fuel the deal is for — as a number from a buyer: 72% over an extension budget across the seasons, with the Strait as its cause. The holder's cure here is not the deal and not a price: an $8bn fuel relief program, which the article sizes at under half the one state's added cost. The buyer's answer to the promise is a crop plan — far less rice, soya because it needs the least input — and a question about how to vote

after the Iran war and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz, fertiliser costs jumped during spring planting (¶13); fuel and fertiliser rose sharply after the war began (¶4)
the $8bn fuel relief program announced last week, after $12bn in 2025 tariff-related aid — split across 50 states, under half of the Arkansas estimate (¶16)

log.what: daily cut over the 10-29 sweep. Forty paragraphs read in full via the cloud fetch; twenty-five scored, none constitutive (no holder on the page; the $8bn program reported by the article, not quoted — declared z null, the aj 10-25 precedent). Object declared on H1c as a farm input — the first Press line with diesel itself as a buyer's number (72% over budget) — with H6 marked at ¶13 and tariffs marked at ¶10, ¶16, ¶23. The sweep missed this page's object (matched on 'midterm' only; the feed carries no opening) — reported in the note. Shoffner stationed with the publication as a candidate, not @O; my call

split.note: one station, two planes: the budget (the article and Loy — diesel, urea, the Strait, the $343m, the $8bn, the bankruptcies: 6–22) and the farm (McKinney and Shoffner — survival, the next generation, the fight: 30–58). The political scientist sits between them (28–32) and reads the predicate against itself: pain may not move a committed vote. Rule 5: McKinney 40 → 46 across two lines on the same object (the farm's future); Shoffner 30 (the numbers) → 58 (the fight) → 34 (the cure) — the oscillation band inside one voice

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: as the US midterms approach, farmers decide what to plant and how to vote
lines.note: THE DOOR: two decisions, one price — the hed names neither the price nor the war
lines.zWhy: a planting decided by cost is a price not yet down

lines.quote: four generations of rice; next year far less rice, a shift to soya because it is cheaper to produce
lines.note: the price as a crop plan — the buyer's answer to the promise
lines.zWhy: far less rice next year is a cost the farm plans around, not past

lines.quote: fuel and fertiliser costs rose sharply after the war on Iran began
lines.note: the cause, dated to the war; 'fuel' is the first of the page's two fuel lines
lines.zWhy: costs up since the war is a cure not yet felt in the field

lines.quote: Democrats expected to gain as voters respond to high prices by switching parties or staying home
lines.note: the gas↔votes predicate (twelfth sighting, the LI corner's first by a non-US desk) — stated as an expectation
lines.zWhy: voters switching on prices is a price costing votes, expected

lines.quote: Texas and Kansas could elect Democratic senators for the first time in decades; Wisconsin's Third and North Carolina's First could decide the House
lines.note: the slate; vacancy on the price
lines.zWhy: two red-state seats read neither way on the diesel line

lines.quote: Shoffner, who quit farming last year, against Cotton — an uphill race centred on costs
lines.note: the slate's Arkansas race with the price as its object; the candidate introduced
lines.zWhy: a race centred on costs is a price not yet down for the candidate's voters

lines.quote: input costs were straining farmers even before the war on Iran
lines.note: the economist dates the strain before the war — the war as the latest cause, not the first
lines.zWhy: a strain before the war is a price the deal was never sized for

lines.quote: the 2018 trade war with China, the Ukraine war, the 2025 tariffs; a drought
lines.note: the causes stacked; tariffs marked (the `tariffs` Reading — window not known to this task)
lines.zWhy: four causes stacked is a price with more than one tap

lines.quote: many switched from rice to soya — the least input-intensive crop, which perhaps can break even
lines.note: 'break even' as the ceiling — the crop plan sized
lines.zWhy: break-even as the hope is a price still above the farm

lines.quote: Arkansas, usually the top rice producer, at its lowest rice acreage since the 1970s; farmers had hoped 2026 would let them return to rice
lines.note: the plan's record — fifty years; the hope dated to this year
lines.zWhy: the lowest acreage since the 1970s is a cost that has already moved the field

lines.quote: after the Iran war hit and the Strait of Hormuz was blocked, fertiliser costs jumped during spring planting
lines.note: H6 MARKED — the Strait as the cause, dated to spring planting; the first page this week to date the farm's price to the water
lines.zWhy: the Strait blocked at planting is the cause of a price the deal does not reach

lines.quote: urea peaked about 39% over budget; diesel ran about 72% above budget across the seasons
lines.note: THE PRICE, AS A BUDGET LINE — diesel itself, the fuel the deal is for: the first Press line with diesel as a buyer's number. The page's lowest line
lines.zWhy: diesel at 72% over budget is the cure's own fuel not yet down

lines.quote: about $343m in added cost for Arkansas alone
lines.note: the price summed for one state
lines.zWhy: $343m for one state is the crunch sized where it lands

lines.quote: Trump announced an $8bn fuel relief program last week, after $12bn in 2025 tariff-related aid; split across 50 states it would cover under half of the Arkansas estimate
lines.note: THE HOLDER'S RELIEF — cash, not a price; dated 'last week'; sized by the article against the cost. The deal is not on the page; this is what is
lines.zWhy: relief under half the cost is a price not come down, paid for instead

lines.quote: welcomed the aid; wants long-term fixes to end this constant battle for survival
lines.note: the buyer's reading of the relief — 'survival' is the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a battle for survival is a price the relief does not end

lines.quote: farm bankruptcies in the first three quarters of 2026 up 19% on 2025 and 73% on 2024 (U of Arkansas National Agricultural Law Center)
lines.note: the record: the crunch as a count
lines.zWhy: bankruptcies up 73% on two years is a cost that has already closed farms

lines.quote: whether farming can remain a sustainable living — heavy things to think about
lines.note: the farm's object: the next generation; the price inside it
lines.zWhy: a living in doubt is a price not yet down for the one who pays it

lines.quote: higher costs, lower crop prices, trade-war and tariff uncertainty made the numbers stop working on 2,000 acres
lines.note: the candidate's own farm as the record; tariffs marked
lines.zWhy: numbers that stopped working is a price that closed a farm last year

lines.quote: if I can't farm, I will fight
lines.note: the candidate's line — the page's most denominated; the price turned into a campaign
lines.zWhy: a fight in place of a farm reads the price as not coming down in time

lines.quote: end the Iran war; predictable trade policy; local processing; a strong Farm Bill
lines.note: THE CHALLENGER'S CURE — end the war, not a deal: the price's cause named as the cure, where the holder names a seller
lines.zWhy: ending the war as the cure is a price read as the war's, not the market's

lines.quote: economic pain may not shift votes; many farmers and rural voters are committed Republicans
lines.note: the predicate's counter — the political scientist reads it against itself
lines.zWhy: a committed vote reads neither way on the diesel line

lines.quote: committed voters see the economy through a partisan lens; not responsive to the agricultural economy
lines.note: the counter restated as a mechanism
lines.zWhy: a partisan lens reads neither way on the diesel line

lines.quote: Farm Journal, April: 35% of farmers who usually vote Republican and 15% who always do were undecided
lines.note: the predicate measured, from the buyer's side (the Fox 10-27 page measured it from the seller's)
lines.zWhy: a third of usual Republicans undecided is a price read as costing votes, by poll

lines.quote: Purdue, September: for the first time this term a majority of surveyed farmers say the country is on the wrong track
lines.note: the predicate measured again, dated to September
lines.zWhy: a wrong track by majority is a price not felt coming down

lines.quote: one of the biggest shifts away from the president's party observed
lines.note: the page's close: the predicate affirmed by the voice that doubted it
lines.zWhy: the biggest shift observed is a price read as costing votes
